reviews.text:
My dogs teeth aren't in the best shape. It is pretty clear that he needs a dental treatment. I asked if I could schedule an appointment for dental treatment straight away. They replied I first need to come by for a consult. So I made an appointment for a consult.

The vet checked my dog for 6 minutes and then told me he needs a dental treatment. To my astonishment she then informed me that they have no availability to schedule an appointment for dental treatment.

€60 for six minutes. That's €600 per hour. To be told I need to make an appointment elsewhere. I tried to work out a reasonable solution with dierenkliniek Amsterdam, but the only suggestions they offered included more invoices.

Staff is nice and tries to be helpful, but in the end dierenkliniek Amsterdam a part of large international chain (Evidencia) committed to profit maximisation and shareholder interest. Your pet's health care comes second.

I had a few good experiences here before, but now my trust had largely eroded.

Update: because of the false portrayal in their response below, I have updated my review from 3 stars to 1 star

I have been going to this chain for 12 years, and every single time I walk out frustrated. The medical care is good in itself, but communication and customer service could be handled even better by a 4-year-old. A specific urine test was supposedly 50 euros. Some time later, the doctor is on the line and he calls 112. I ask if that is the final price. "Certainly," he says. Then I go to drop off the urine, and after searching for the price for 10 minutes, she comes back and quotes a figure of 168. So the original price that was quoted was one-third of the actual price. Furthermore, it seems that every time I go there, it's not a blonde's day, because I get a grumpy face from here to Tokyo.

Edit: I did receive a call from the doctor in question today with his apologies. Very polite, considering most people don't do this anymore these days.

Unfortunately, I cannot give 0 stars.

No personal attention, no care, and little empathy for the animal. It feels like a factory where the focus is mainly on how to earn more money through unnecessary medication and procedures.

Unfortunately, the welfare of the animal does not seem to be the number one priority here.

The service has been terrible for the last 2 years; they are not there for the animals, but for the money.
The employees behind the counter are like children who don't know what they are doing and therefore give incorrect information and make incorrect entries in vaccination booklets. They are also very rude.
I have been going there for 50 years and have never been treated so shabbily.
Came on time but always waiting I don’t know why

Wow, I have never received such poor care anywhere as I have here. Even other clinics indicate that it is simply unacceptable that no help is offered here when your pet is in bad shape.

I sent an email about this some time ago, but I never received a response. That only confirms to me how little they apparently care.
It used to be quite a nice clinic. Now they don't care at all how your animal is doing, they don't help, they don't think along, nothing. Very unpleasant..

This clinic is part of Evidensia! Check these articles in the Media:

bnnvara
Love for animals as a revenue model at Evidensia and Anicura
The rates at Evidensia are much higher than at independent veterinarians. Emergency consultations can run up to approximately €270. The municipality...

Oct 25, 2025

NRC
Another intervention at veterinary chain Evidensia: new director leaves again after six months
Another intervention at veterinary chain Evidensia: new director leaves again after six months ... Private equity Former Philips executive Arjen...

Disappointing experience.

My cat was neutered at this practice and underwent a comprehensive health check at the time. During that visit, the necessary checks were performed, and I have already paid a hefty bill.

Just four weeks later, I returned for a second vaccination. When making the appointment, I understood that I would only pay for the vaccination. To my surprise, I received a bill of €68.24 for a vaccination and another consultation.

What bothers me most is that this was not clearly communicated beforehand. As a customer, I expect transparency regarding costs. Additionally, during the consultation, I did not feel that much new information was being checked. The veterinarian spent a long time on the computer, asked questions that I thought were already in the file, and was typing a lot. As a result, I did not get the feeling that the extra time was actually being spent on my cat.

Because my cat had already been fully examined and declared healthy just four weeks earlier, I even asked if there might be something wrong. The long consultation gave me the impression that there was a problem, even though that ultimately turned out not to be the case.

I understand that veterinarians incur costs, but €68.24 for a vaccination appointment so soon after a previous health check feels disproportionate to me. Because of this experience, I do not feel taken seriously as a customer and will think carefully before making another appointment here.

Warning: Significantly higher costs and fragmented care since Evidensia takeover

I was a client at this clinic for years but recently switched to another veterinarian. The difference in approach and costs is enormous:
- Abdominal ultrasound: €350 here vs €160-220 elsewhere in Amsterdam
- Cardiac ultrasound: €500 here (referred to Evidensia location) vs €250 elsewhere
- Standard medication: 5-10% more expensive than other clinics

Treatment approach:
The clinic works with fragmented diagnostics: first one test, then a separate appointment for the next test, repeated visits over and over. This quickly adds up in both costs and stress for the animal. At my new vet, everything is discussed and planned in one go, much more efficient and animal-friendly.

Worst-case scenario pressure tactics:
Most recently, after bloodwork (another €400), the vet immediately suggested my cat likely had cancer. When I asked what else it could be, he insisted it was “very likely cancer” and recommended an immediate €350 ultrasound. At my new vet, the ultrasound was €220, and a simple blood pressure check revealed the actual cause: hypertension, not cancer. Using worst-case scenarios to pressure clients into expensive tests without discussing other possibilities is, in my view, unacceptable.

Euthanasia recommendations:
Over the years, euthanasia was recommended multiple times for my cat, who is now 16 years old and still enjoying life. These repeated suggestions, while my cat was doing fine, severely damaged my trust.

Sedation for routine examinations:
It was regularly suggested that my cat be sedated for routine examinations “due to resistance.” Of course, you pay more for that, too. At my new vet, this turned out to be completely unnecessary, they simply know how to handle cats properly.

Positive exception:
Veterinarian Elena was always excellent, knowledgeable, caring, and realistic in her recommendations.

Since the Evidensia takeover, costs have increased dramatically without any improvement in quality of care. I now pay half as much at another clinic for the same treatments, with better communication and less stress for my animals. For chronically ill pets or clients without insurance, I strongly recommend comparing prices with other Amsterdam clinics before committing to expensive diagnostics or treatments here.

I went with my cat last Thursday. They used to be good, but now they are worthless and expensive. My cat eats a lot and is skin and bones; she had a blood test. Not much came of it; I was told to come back in 4 weeks to have her weighed again. This cost me nearly 243 euros. I went to Veterinarian Purmerend today (highly recommended; the vet takes their time and is honest. It is large, clean, bright, and dogs and cats have separate waiting rooms).
There, a large, hard lump was discovered during the examination (apparently, the vet from the Spaardammer hadn't felt this during her examination).
It is cancer, and there is a very small chance that it is on the spleen. I am having an ultrasound done anyway; if it isn't right, I will have her put to sleep immediately.
For the lengthy examination involving fluid administration, medication, and consultation, I spent 96 euros.
I got almost an immediate appointment for an emergency situation for my cat. The veterinarian later called me and explained me everything very clearly. The lady at the desk was also very helpful.

Recently, my kitten Asher received emergency treatment at this veterinary clinic following a severe chest injury. With about 25 stitches and multiple check-ups and follow-up appointments later, I can happily say: he is doing completely fine again.

I have been coming here for years with my other cat, sometimes for emergencies and sometimes for routine care, and I have experience with multiple veterinarians, including at other locations. That is precisely why I am surprised by some of the negative reviews. In fact, my experiences have been very positive time and again. The veterinarians are skilled and professional, and the rest of the staff is always friendly, committed, and helpful.
As far as I am concerned, they truly provide top-notch care. The dedication and commitment I see here deserve appreciation rather than criticism. I can therefore wholeheartedly recommend this clinic – your pet is undoubtedly in good hands here!
My feline friends are in good hands here.

My cats have been coming here since I've had them, 10 years now. However, today I called because one of my cats has barely eaten for three days. All they said was that they were full and would be there tomorrow too. At one of the locations, there wasn't even a vet present today. How is that possible? You have three locations and nowhere is there room? I find this truly absurd and wonder what's going on with this clinic, given the other reviews. You can't even make an appointment online for the coming weeks. And then they mention that you have a client freeze to "provide the necessary care to existing clients." Not at all! Very strange and worrying, but especially awful for your pet. I'm going to look for another clinic.

Thank you so much!

Sem

My experience was good in the beginning for basic needs but has gotten progressively worse over the last year. My cat has recurring dental issues (dental resorption) and when I told the vet that she had stopped eating because she had a tooth that had visible resorption past the gum line, she told that it was not possible because one bad tooth ''does not cause enough pain'' for her to not eat. Their lead time for any dental work was three months and they also wanted to do a 400€ ultrasound instead, which for a cat that is also anxious would have to be sedated for 100+€. And for what, a dental issue? I have since gone to a different vet who was able to remove the tooth within two weeks and she has had a voracious appetite since. An important lesson in advocating for your own pets when needed.

On a separate occasion I ran out of prescription cat food that they carry and went first thing in the morning to try and get a couple of cans until my order came in. They had none and said they would call me back when they had it in stock. They never called me back and wanted to send me to vets in west that would maybe have it. If you are in need of Purina Pro Plan Veterinary Diets EN Gastrointestinal, Ranzijn is the place, not a random vet in west which they should have known. Care and customer service has only gotten progressively worse and I have since switched vets.
A very nice animal clinic ♡
Please fix your phone system. 45min minimum waiting on the line not moving forward or ending on an endless bip, each time for an appointment is so annoying. I can't even imagine for an emergency..

Terrible place; I have been a customer here for a while and have actually always had very unpleasant experiences. They are extremely focused on money and often do not have experts on staff who can diagnose accurately. I visited multiple times with my cat for a lump on her nose, which they squeezed out several times, and then sent me away under the pretext of an infection. That is why I went to a vet in the east of the country, who immediately recognized it as a tumor and surgically removed it.

I recently visited again for sedatives, for which they stated they are only allowed to provide them if a consultation is linked to it (meaning I have to shell out an extra €50), without any legal basis. They also once charged me a weekend rate without discussing this beforehand, even though I came on the weekend at their request instead of the week before. In short, people who unfortunately choose money over anything and show absolutely no consideration for fellow citizens who are less well-off (see also their policy regarding the city pass vouchers; disgusting).

WARNING!!!

This used to be a good vet clinic, but since it was taken over by Evidensia, the experience has really gone downhill. It felt like they cared more about hitting monthly targets than about the clients and the animals.
I recently took my cat there and immediately got a bad vibe. Afterward I mentioned it to the owner of the pet shop I always go to, and she told me she had also stopped using this clinic and recommended a different vet.
I went to the other vet and the difference was huge: they were genuinely friendly and caring toward both me and my cat, and the bill ended up being about 50% less for a similar visit and treatment . Based on my experience, I wouldn’t recommend this clinic anymore.
My cat loves this doctor. 5/5!
It's a veterinary practice

The team at Dierenkliniek saved our sweet cat’s life. He had a urinary tract blockage, and they acted quickly, communicated clearly, and most importantly, helped Teddy make a full recovery. Their rehabilitation care was excellent, and they provided clear instructions and medication to support his healing. We are incredibly grateful for their hard work, compassion, and the exceptional care they gave our fur baby.

Extremely disappointed, they always forget to update you on when vaccines are to be renewed, lab tests that are basic and done in house rather than actually doing research to see what is wrong with your dog.

For repeated problems, instead of testing for real causes, they push for their own product. Sad since they used to be good, now it’s another money seeking vet store with employees who push for products and profits rather than taking care of your pets.

The service wants the best, you go with a sick dog, they prescribe medicine, you pay for the appointment, the dog is allergic to their drug, you call, come with the dog and you pay for the appointment again due to their fault because they don't care if the dog is sensitive or allergic to drugs, they just do business.. but unfortunately there is no choice.. Last year the dog almost died, the dog had a rubber ball in its intestines that it swallowed, the dog was dying and they prescribed an antibiotic and a painkiller... it's terrible, they are not responsible for the prescribed drugs, they prescribed other drugs today, if the dog gets an allergy, do I have to make a third request to be prescribed another drug and pay for the appointment again? And so on ad infinitum? Be responsible for the life and safety of animals, and care if the dog is allergic to drugs, read the dossier).
Great animal clinic, one of the few in the area that also treats rodents.

Thank you so much!

Sem

During my first life-threatening situation, I was completely abandoned. After I heard that it was a dangerous situation for my cat, they said they were fully booked. No help or alternative was offered. Other unfamiliar clinics helped me better than my own veterinarian. I cancelled my registration immediately, and even there, the response pointed the finger at me for not calling sooner. I called in the morning as soon as it was clear something was wrong. Unprofessional and, above all, zero empathy.

Last minute cancellation because their vet got sick. I think it’s unecceptable and you need to have a replacement available. They also never have spots for the clients if animal got sick and needs urgent visit same day, as other vet clinics always have.

Thanks for the review!

Sem

Early years were good practice. Quality has declined in recent years. Ordered medications are not delivered without notification, are sent from location to location, and several locations have closed without notice.

They gave me two wrong pet passports and refused to enter the rabies vaccination information in my passports. I had to go to another, competent veterinarian to fix their mess. Save your money – this is a very disorganized veterinary practice.

I have been bringing my cats here for 3 years. In the last year we came almost every 2-3 months because of several reasons and each time I asked them if anything else was due, any shots/vaccinations etc. They always said no. A week ago I noticed that my cats’ rabies vaccinations have actually expired by 4-5 months now even though they always said no. I called to make an appointment and asked them to at least cover the costs of renewing the titration tests for traveling abroad since they also have become invalid because of this gap that occurred due to their fault. It’s already bad enough that my babies and I have to go through this whole process again. They said they were going to check this with their manager. 1 week after I came to my appointment and this was still not checked. They expect me to spend even more money at a place that caused this without even knowing if it will be covered. After such mistake they don’t even show the courtesy of handling such a simple request on a timely manner or at least inform me before my appointment that it was not discussed yet. I always came here and spent so much money on all the treatments of my cats for years and the result is this. Will change vets and start working with a more professional place.

A very bad situation. Since it was sold, this veterinary clinic has gone downhill significantly. The story goes as follows: I called the clinic urgently to report that my cat was doing very poorly and was more dead than alive. According to the veterinary assistant, there was no availability, regular consultations had to continue that day, and emergencies could not be squeezed in. We were told to just call another vet or try a home visit. It is truly ridiculous that people and animals are treated this way. I recommend never going to this veterinary clinic again because they do not care about people or animals at all.
Trustworthy. Your pet is assured of the best care, they're in safe hands here.

Apparently, an emergency appointment can't be made because it can only be made on the day itself? Should I just find another vet since there are plenty in Amsterdam? Come on, you haven't organized your schedule, and the vets are working overtime like headless chickens to benefit investors.

The doctors here are so exceptionally kind and patient. They really took their time with us and went over everything immediately. Our (often quite scared) cat was relatively at ease and experienced minimal stress thanks to the gentle approach.

We usually visit the Rembrandtpark loc but unfortunately had to come for ultrasounds.

At pickup this afternoon, I asked if the vet said anything about the results. The older receptionist lady, who'd been chatting with my bf, switched to an angry voice and said, "Why would I know? I'm not the vet" then stared at her computer silently. I said, "Oh, is it not in the records...?" She immediately raised her voice, telling me to give her a minute.

When she read the results, I just said "oh okay" a few times, avoiding questions in case she further escalated. Then she said TWICE, loudly, "If you think I'm lying, you can call the vet." ??????

Then she spoke to my bf again in a friendly voice -- telling him his "bad vibes" (stress) are harming our cat -- without acknowledging my presence again. Weirdly rude & unprofessional.

Unfortunately, this veterinary clinic has changed over the last 4 years since the departure of the older veterinarians; it has become distant and businesslike, and for example, there are no more evening consultations! This is my story: I have been bringing my cats to this clinic for 20 years. This time, my cat came out of the emergency clinic very sick with little chance of recovery, especially since he wasn't taking medication and was in a lot of pain as a result. We decided very quickly that we didn't want any further treatment and wanted to have euthanasia performed that very same day. The practice assistant said there was no time for that and advised me to start 'calling around'. Because, of course, no practice does that without knowing a cat, I called again after fifteen minutes to beg if it really wasn't possible. There were three veterinarians present, none of whom wanted to make time. A nightmare. I found an incredibly sweet veterinarian who eventually did it at our home. I will never go there again.

I adopted the sweetest but stupidest cat ever, who is obsessed with eating things he cannot digest. When I saw my cat vomiting again yesterday while crying, I thought it might be the last time. But the staff at Dierenkliniek Amsterdam are always there for us. From start to finish (and everything in between, like the glass of water I received when I dropped off my cat in tears), thank you for all the kind and good care.
I really hope I never have to come back for surgery again, but if I have to, I have complete confidence in you!
Amazing people, very sweet and always there for my dog ​​Kenzo. Thank you for all your support ❣️❤️

It used to be a good clinic, but in my opinion, not anymore. I called twice this morning regarding a very sick cat. I live a 5-minute walk from the clinic, but I couldn't come in for an emergency. According to the assistant, I could go to another clinic in the afternoon. Since I had no transport and the cat was so sick, I tried to make an appointment anyway. I was flatly turned away. It basically came down to me having to figure it out myself, at least that's the feeling I got. I panicked; the poor thing wasn't doing well, and it's all over for me right now. Fortunately, I called a vet who acted immediately.
super nice people and they looked at the cat with attention, they did a thorough examination which feels good
We are very satisfied with this animal clinic. Two days ago, they took excellent care of our dear Tyra. Every other time we've been there, we've always received prompt and friendly service.
Great clinic with knowledgeable staff, only the current prices are painful :-(

This has been my vet for years because they’re less bad than other vets in the city. However I’m most disappointed because this week I walked twice from Houthavens to find the place closed both times; first, they changed their closing times to 6pm BUT NEVER INFORMED THE CLIENTS; moreover, for sickness of personnel, today they decided to close at 5pm.. who in their right mind would not stay open just another hour but decide instead to create a bad service incident?
We managed to free up a spot at the last minute on a busy day! The veterinarian was very friendly, knowledgeable, and interested. A very pleasant experience for us and the dog.
I was scared as this was my kitty first doctor visit but the vet was super kind and professional, treated my baby with much love !! Definitely gonna keep coming for anything that we need.
My dog ​​had a grass hair in his eye. Our vet treated him quickly (emergency).🐕 …

This vet clinic near Amsterdam Marina was fantastic! My business partner and I brought his dog here and were met with warm smiles and exceptional care. The staff was friendly, professional, and clearly passionate about animals. A truly great experience—highly recommended!

Came here for years with my cat and the experience was good, but when I got a rescue dog who was anxious and needed a bit more care, I was very let down. I didn’t feel like anyone took the time and space to cater for her, unless you can come in with your pet and get the job done fast without wasting a second of their time, it’s not going to work here. I find this disappointing, as it’s quite common for pets to have a bit of anxiety or fear around the vet. The attitude from the people working here was not understanding and caring at all. We moved to another vet and the experience was totally different. I came back to review here after hearing from a friend that they had the same experience, I think it’s important to write reviews like this so that people can have the chance to read it before choosing this vet, and the business can have a chance to improve.

Very good. Went there urgently regarding the cat. Practice open until 10:00 PM. Nice space. Took their time for the examination. Super sweet to the cat. Medication available there and given to take home. Despite everything, Lenthe felt safe at the vet, was very calm and not afraid. I live in the Jordaan, so it's too far for me. A pity. Thank you for the good care.

My dog has a recurring ear infection and I have visited this clinic 3x only for them to do the same - check ears and give the same medication - instead of actually checking what the problem is as it might probably be allergies. They didn’t even so a specimen check as opposed to the vet we went to in Prague and Germany.

Another thing is I brought my bunny for emergency check up and they told me that the teeth was ok so they were unsure what it actually was. They ended up giving my bunny a pain reliever shot and critical care. I was expecting that since they were unsure, they would require blood tests etc but no. The next day my bunny died.

I recently changed vet and the current one we have is so much better. I didn’t even know that my other bunny has something on her teeth (but nothing serious) until the new vet told me. Dierenkliniek Amsterdam never mentioned this to me when I had my bunnies’ annual vaccination and check up with them.
Very good

After 14 years, I'm beyond disappointed and not even worth a star.
Last year, at the start of COVID, my dog ​​became deaf after treatment with medication I never agreed to.
They said it would be okay. It wasn't, he still barely hears.
I called this morning because my dog ​​seems to be having terrible back pain. I didn't feel like going back to this practice, but then again, my dog ​​has been known there since birth.
First of all, I was shocked at how rude and unfriendly the phone was.
Then I was told I couldn't use a city pass voucher because I wouldn't get it until Monday. "That's not allowed retroactively," she said. Bullshit. For years, I've only brought the voucher the next day. I don't know in advance when my dog ​​will get sick!!! It's always been treated this way. I'm allowed to come in, but I have to pay for everything myself, I'm told, and oh yeah, there's a weekend fee on top of that. When I asked why it was all about money, the woman hung up the phone.
I'm shocked!!!
How can such a socially responsible and well-established practice deteriorate so drastically and become so bad within just a few years?!? Back when Dr. Peeters was still available to see him daily, now you only see his colleagues and successors.
It's more like an automated factory now, where you have to spend as much money as possible in as little time as possible.
No one listens anymore. There's no time for that. Off to the counter, pay up, and get out of here.
Deeply sad. While Dr. Peeters used to always be a listening ear for the less fortunate, you only see him now if you have a deep wallet.
I've referred dozens of people (animals) to Dr. Peeters over the past 14 years. That would certainly not happen again. Moreover, I would advise everyone not to go to the Westerpark Veterinary Clinic anymore, unless you have a deep wallet.
The new name, Westerpark Veterinary Clinic (formerly just Dr. Peeters Veterinarian) has changed quite a bit.
Not for me anymore, anyway. You don't just hang up the phone during a conversation.

The vet is really experienced and professional. My 7 month old dog was very sick, and she was very assertive with the first diagnosis. Also, immediate treatment was given to my puppy to stabilize her. Luna had to be hospitalized and the Vet …

We had just moved to Amsterdam and didn't have a vet yet. Our dog had a little accident in the park and hurt her nail/paw. We called and were able to get an appointment right away. The vet in question was just about to go home but decided …

I went there about 8 years ago with my cat and two small dogs. Expensive, little expert advice, and unfriendly. Every time I was there, things went in a strange way: rushed, worthless advice, with no attention to my animals. Hopeless and …
